Sources and coverage

South Korea uses vuski/admdongkor, July 2026. This data is derived from administrative-dong boundaries released by Statistics Korea SGIS under KOGL Type 1, modified by vuski/admdongkor, distributed under CC BY 4.0.

Districts within ordinary cities are combined into their parent cities. Autonomous metropolitan districts remain separate. Sejong has no second-level division. Jeju’s two administrative cities are included. The July 2026 snapshot includes the Jeonnam–Gwangju merger.

North Korea uses OpenStreetMap administrative relations, clipped to OpenStreetMap coastlines. © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0. These are mapped boundaries; recent changes may not yet be represented.

Coastline vertices are retained without simplification. Province outlines are derived from the same subdivision geometry. English names use OpenStreetMap and the South Korea maps dataset. Flags: flag-icons (MIT).
